title: Δελφῖνες καὶ φάλαιναι καὶ κωβιός
titleEn: The Dolphins, the Whales, and the Goby
part: The Dolphins, the Whales, and the Goby (Chambry 95 · Perry 62)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 95 (= Perry 62). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Δελφῖνες καὶ φάλαιναι πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐμάχοντο.
sentences.tr: Delphines kai phalainai pros allēlous emachonto.
sentences.l: Dolphins and whales were fighting against one another.

sentences.t: Ἐπὶ πολὺ δὲ τῆς διαφορᾶς σφοδρυνομένης, κωβιὸς ἀνέδυ (ἔστι δὲ οὗτος μικρὸς ἰχθύς) καὶ ἐπειρᾶτο αὐτοὺς διαλύειν.
sentences.tr: Epi poly de tēs diaphoras sphodrynomenēs, kōbios anedy (esti de houtos mikros ichthys) kai epeirato autous dialyein.
sentences.l: And the quarrel growing violent for a long while, a goby came up (this creature is a small fish) and tried to part them.
sentences.i: And as the quarrel grew fiercer and dragged on, a goby came up — it is a small fish — and tried to part them.
sentences.n: Genitive absolute once more, present: while the quarrel intensifies. σφοδρύνομαι, 'to become σφοδρός, violent', is a rare verb. The remark in parentheses is an aside for a reader who may not know how small a κωβιός is; the whole fable turns on that. ἀνέδυ is a root aorist, active in form but intransitive in sense: he came up out of the water.

sentences.t: Εἷς δέ τις τῶν δελφίνων ὑποτυχὼν ἔφη πρὸς αὐτόν· « Ἀλλ᾽ ἡμῖν ἀνεκτότερόν ἐστι μαχομένους ὑπ᾽ ἀλλήλων διαφθαρῆναι ἢ σοῦ διαλλακτοῦ τυχεῖν. »
sentences.tr: Heis de tis tōn delphinōn hypotychōn ephē pros auton· « All’ hēmin anektoteron esti machomenous hyp’ allēlōn diaphtharēnai ē sou diallaktou tychein. »
sentences.l: But a certain one of the dolphins, taking-up-the-word, said to him: « But it is more endurable for us, fighting, to be destroyed by one another than to get you for a reconciler. »
sentences.i: But one of the dolphins took up the word and said to him: « We can better bear fighting it out and being destroyed by one another than getting you for a peacemaker. »
sentences.n: ὑποτυχών is the house rendering 'taking-up-the-word' — replying, not any physical seizing. μαχομένους is accusative, agreeing with the unexpressed subject of the infinitive. τυγχάνω takes a genitive of what one obtains, σοῦ διαλλακτοῦ, 'you as a reconciler'. The insult is that his good offices would be worse than the deaths.

sentences.t: Οὕτως ἔνιοι τῶν ἀνθρώπων οὐδενὸς ἄξιοι ὄντες, ὅταν ταραχῆς λάβωνται, δοκοῦσί τινες εἶναι.
sentences.tr: Houtōs enioi tōn anthrōpōn oudenos axioi ontes, hotan tarachēs labōntai, dokousi tines einai.
sentences.l: Thus some among men, being worth nothing, whenever they lay hold of a disturbance, seem to be somebodies.
sentences.i: Thus some men who are worth nothing seem to be persons of consequence whenever they can lay hold of a disturbance.
sentences.n: λαμβάνομαι in the middle takes a genitive of what is grasped. ὅταν with the subjunctive is indefinite, 'whenever it happens'. τινες carries its full weight here — not merely 'some' but 'somebodies, people who count'.
